title: Osteoporosis — overview
claims: Women lose bone rapidly in the first few years after the menopause.
Women are more at risk of osteoporosis than men, particularly if menopause begins before the age of 45 or if the ovaries have been removed.
The NHS lists not exercising regularly, low body mass index, heavy drinking, smoking, long-term steroid tablets and some other medicines or conditions as risk factors.
The NHS advises getting enough vitamin D from sunlight in summer and from a supplement in winter; a doctor may prescribe a vitamin D supplement all year round.
